recipes.name: Baked Beans
ingredients_raw: 2 (15 ounce) cans baked beans with pork

steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine canned beans with pork, brown sugar, onion, ketchup, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a 9-inch square baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until sauce is thickened and bacon is cooked, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Beans
raw_recipe.description: A little sweet, a little spicy! Canned pork 'n beans are taken to new heights with the addition of bacon, brown sugar, onion, and a few basic condiments.

review.reviewBody: These beans are great! I only used 1/4 cup each of brown sugar and ketchup, so there was no problem with it being "runny". I also cooked 4 slices of bacon then chopped it and mixed it in. That way I could use more bacon, but keep the grease out.

This was a good base. I followed the instructions exactly the first time and modified the next and was pleasantly surprised. I ran out of the pork and beans cans from the first attempt. I soaked pinto beans overnight. I had pork shoulder chunked up and deforested so I took about 3 oz and cut it into about 1/2 inch bits and cooked that and 1 lb of bacon in the same cast iron until nearly crispy. I added the onion to the mixture and when the bacon was crispy and onions caramelized, I removed the heat and added the brown sugar, about 1/4 teaspoon of chipotle chili pepper, 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1/8 teaspoon of Mexican chili powder and 1/8 teaspoon of cayenne. I put this mixture and the rest of the ingredients into my instant pot so as to not take chances with raw beans. Pressure cooked for 1 hr 20mins. Very delicious, a huge hit.

This was delicious! I did change it a bit. I used (2) 28 oz cans of plain baked beans, undrained. I baked 1 pound of bacon in the oven until done, then chopped it up into small pieces. I poured the bacon grease in a frying pan. I chopped a large onion and a large green bell pepper, and sauteed them in the bacon grease for 5 minutes. (Next time I might add 1 chopped jalapeno to the onions and green bell pepper.) Then added 2 T of minced garlic and sauteed another 2 minutes. I put everything in a large bowl. I added 1/2 cup ketchup, 1/2 cup yellow mustard, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 2 teas chili powder, 1 teas garlic powder, 1 T worchestershire sauce, 1/4 teas cayenne. Mixed it all well and poured it in a 9x13 pyrex baking dish. I baked it covered about 7 hours at 275 degrees, then took off the foil and baked for 1 more hour uncovered. Could be cooked in less time at 300 degrees. So yummy!

I used Bush's Brown Sugar and Bacon baked beans, added maple pancake syrup to mixture and used BBQ sauce (no Ketchup). I made this for a company potluck, so use a slow-cooker vs. oven, and everyone was asking me for recipe! In slow cooker, cook on low for 3 hours or high for 2 hours.

Thought this was a good base for making it your own. I used ham, because I had some leftover ham I needed to use. Also switched out the ketchup for molasses, and put it all in the crock pot instead of baking. I also used 1/4 cup coconut sugar instead of brown sugar.
For the last hour of the cooking, I left the lid off of the crock pot, this allowed some of the moisture to escape, and made a thicker sauce. Will make again.

I used the recipe but made it my own. I used 2 cans of tri blend beans instead but kept the other ingredients the same. I also simmered it on the stove. The flavor was excellent. I love this simple, easy recipe that is exploding with flavor.

Very tasty beans! I cut back on the ketchup but added a little molasses and some liquid smoke. Since I did not use the bacon, I didn't have to be concerned about it crisping, so I didn't have to keep it in the oven for an hour. I've found similar recipes on this site, and 35 min or so (without the bacon to cook) worked fine. You get the same or better quality with preparing beans this way then using the dry beans. Saves time and effort. Thanks for this great recipe!

I used 2 19 oz. cans Campbell's pork an beans, 1/2 the sugar, the rest of the recipe. I wasn't sure weather to cover while baking. I didn't have much liquid in my mix so covered after 30 min as it looked to be getting dry. Also, chopped up SIX pieces of bacon and mixed in. Yummy!

Awesome base recipe for easy baked beans. I double everything except for the brown sugar. I used bacon end pieces I get from a local butcher and fry them first with the onion before adding. I also drained the extra juice from the canned beans.

I've done baked beans using almost this same recipe for a long time but as I was usually making it for maybe 15 to 20 people I doubled all the ingredients plus I added maybe a half cup of barbeque sauce which I think adds to the flavor. I used baked beans in a can so I also drained as much of the sauce/juice from the cans so it wouldn't be too soupy.
Made this recently, added 6 slices of bacon and cooked in crock pot on high for 3 hours, was delicious. Will definitely make again.

I did make some changes. I fried the bacon a head of time and used 1/2 lb of thick bacon, then crumbled it into the beans. I drained off the water from the top of the bean can. I used Bushes baked beans Original. I has no pork. Several people asked for the recipe!

Made these for Memorial Day. So good I am going to make them again for a July 4th BBQ. Only change I made was that I used apple cider vinegar as I didn't have red wine vinegar. Delicious and easy to make.
I love this recipe. Instead of using canned baked beans, I use canned pork & beans.
This is a quick and easy recipe. Anybody could do it. Is quick is easy and I made no changes

Fantastic! Cooked bacon and chopped into bites before mixing it in the beans. Used a little less brown sugar and catsup than called for, since the canned beans I used also featured brown sugar. I used to think doctoring up canned beans was "cheating," but these were such a hit that I won't tell if you don't. ;-)
I use bbq/ketchup mixture and a little extra mustard. They are really good. My family asks me to make them for gatherings.
Easy!! I used 1/2 lb. dried navy beans, reserving a small amount of the cooking liquid for the sauce. Then followed the recipe, adding a slice of pineapple chopped fine. Will make again.
Put a couple more slices of bacon in it.
sooo sweet could not get through the first bite
